references.text: The immediate context where Jesus describes how the crowd can interpret weather signs – clouds from the west mean rain, and a south wind means heat – yet still cannot interpret the signs of the times ([ref:Luk 12:54-55|Luke 12:54-55]).

The parallel in [ref:Matt 16:1-4|Matthew 16:1-4] where the Pharisees and Sadducees ask for a sign from heaven, and Jesus rebukes them because they can interpret the appearance of the sky but not the signs of the times (τὰ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν).

In [ref:Matt 16:3|Matthew 16:3] Jesus uses almost identical wording: "You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but you cannot interpret the signs of the times" – a direct parallel to Luke 12:56.

In [ref:1 Krøn 12:32|1 Chronicles 12:32] the sons of Issachar are described as men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do – an example of the ability to "interpret the times" that Jesus calls for.

In [ref:Matt 24:32-33|Matthew 24:32-33] Jesus uses the parable of the fig tree: when its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near – again an encouragement to read the signs of the times.
In [ref:Rom 12:2|Romans 12:2] the related word δοκιμάζειν is used for "testing" what is God's will – the same ability for spiritual discernment (δοκιμάζειν) that Jesus seeks in Luke 12:56.

In [ref:Luk 19:44|Luke 19:44] Jesus weeps over Jerusalem because they did not know their time of visitation (τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου) – a consequence of precisely this lack of ability to judge the times (καιρός).

The word ὑποκριταί (hypocrites) is repeatedly used by Jesus to rebuke the religious leaders, as in [ref:Matt 23:13|Matthew 23:13], where hypocrisy consists in pretending to serve God without truly doing so.

In [ref:1 Tess 5:1-2|1 Thessalonians 5:1-2] Paul speaks of "times and seasons" (χρόνων καὶ καιρῶν) and emphasizes that the day of the Lord will come like a thief – believers should therefore know the character of the times.

In [ref:Dan 12:3|Daniel 12:3] it is spoken of the wise who shall shine – and in [ref:Dan 12:10|Daniel 12:10] that the wise shall understand while the wicked do not, which reflects the contrast between those who interpret the signs of the times and those who do not.
